metadata.title: NH3 Emission Factors for Synthetic Fertilizer Application to Fields
metadata.description: Ammonia emission factors for different types of synthetic (mineral) fertilizers applied to fields. Values represent kg NH3-N per kg N applied (2015-2017 period).
metadata.unit: kg NH3-N per kg N applied
metadata.note: NH3 contributes to acidification and eutrophication but is not a direct greenhouse gas. Must be converted to kg NH3 by multiplying by (17/14) = 1.214.
metadata.footnote: Sulfur-coated ammonium and amide-containing fertilizers have been subject to regulations since 2020 to limit ammonia volatilization.

ammoniumsulfat.name: Ammoniumsulfat (svovlsur ammoniak)
ammoniumsulfat.note: Subject to regulations since 2020 to limit NH3 volatilization

calcium_ammonium_nitrat.name: Calcium ammonium nitrat
calcium_ammonium_nitrat.description: Calcium ammonium nitrate (most common fertilizer in Denmark)

urea.name: Urea
urea.note: Subject to regulations since 2020 to limit NH3 volatilization

default_factor.name: Weighted average for Danish synthetic fertilizers
default_factor.description: Default factor to use when specific fertilizer type is unknown. Calculated as weighted average based on 2017 consumption (248.7 tons N total).

conversion.description: To convert kg NH3-N to kg NH3, multiply by 17/14 = 1.214
conversion.example: If emission factor is 0.026 kg NH3-N/kg N, then in kg NH3: 0.026 * 1.214 = 0.0316 kg NH3/kg N

usage_notes: These factors apply to synthetic (mineral) fertilizers only, not organic fertilizers (manure)
For organic fertilizers (husdyrgødning), use separate emission factors from Table 19
NH3 emissions from fertilizer application are separate from livestock NH3 emissions
Default factor (0.026 kg NH3-N/kg N) is recommended when specific fertilizer type is unknown
Emissions occur during and shortly after application (volatilization)
Actual emissions depend on application method, timing, weather, and soil conditions
